children: , the diabetes and obesity drugmaker, fell 0.59% to $1,409.21 at 10:00 a.m. ET on November 2, even as Cantor Fitzgerald raised its price target to $1,600 from $1,440 and maintained Overweight. The higher target puts pricing power in focus: demand is climbing fast, but Lilly is collecting less on realized prices.

Lilly's October 29 results showed quarterly revenue of $24.397 billion, with Mounjaro generating $10.723 billion and Zepbound adding $5.352 billion. Together, the two medicines supplied 65.9% of revenuea powerful growth engine that also concentrates the business around its metabolic franchise. Worldwide volume rose 53%, while realized prices fell 15%. Full-year revenue guidance stands at $91 billion$92 billion, making the balance between expanding demand and pricing pressure a key test.

The GuruFocus snapshot gives Lilly a GF Score of 97/100, with profitability and growth standing out against softer financial-strength and momentum readings. Yet a price-to-earnings ratio of 46.30 suggests investors are already paying for substantial earnings expectations. Cantor's 11.1% target increase signals confidence, but the operating test remains clear: whether rising volumes and product mix can keep supporting earnings as realized prices retreat. Strong demand could sustain the growth story; durable profitability will determine how much of that growth reaches shareholders.

title: Eli Lilly Stocks Move Lower With Higher Target Facing a Volume-Price Tradeoff
